subject: early-literacy
title: Hearing the first sound in a word
summary: Listen for the sound at the start of a word and match words that begin the same way.

lesson.text: For a parent, older brother or sister, or anyone helping a young child: say every word out loud. This lesson is about listening.
Say a word slowly and stretch the first sound: mmm... ango. The sound you hear first is the beginning sound. For mango it is m.

lesson.title: Find the first sound
steps: Now say "sand" and "soap". They start with s too.

lesson.text: Say three words: "pen, pot, cup". Ask which one starts with a different sound. The answer is cup, because pen and pot start with p.
Use the child's own name: "Your name, Tobi, starts with t. What else starts with t?"

questions.prompt: What is the first sound in "mango"?
questions.explanation: Stretch it: mmm... ango. The first sound is m.

questions.prompt: Which word starts with the same sound as "sun"?
questions.explanation: Sun and soap both start with s. Table starts with t, milk with m, pen with p.

questions.prompt: Which is the odd one out: pen, pot, cup, plate?
questions.explanation: Pen, pot and plate all start with p. Cup starts with c, so it is the odd one out.
Say it slowly: t... omato. The first sound is t, like table and tap.
